pr_title: Fix crash when "show folder sizes" is enabled
pr_body:
**Resolved / Related Issues**
Items resolved / related issues by this PR.
- Closes #8413
- Removes some unused Helper classes 

**Details of Changes**
Add details of changes here.
The issue seems to be due to the fact that the file list is changed on a background thread (in `ApplyFilesAndFoldersChangesAsync()`) while it's being enumerated in `UpdateSelectionSize()`.
This PR adds a "thread-safe" enumerator to fix this issue. Alternative could have been returning a copy of the list (with ToList()) as in [1e758ef](https://github.com/files-community/Files/pull/8716/commits/1e758ef2cda59a5c74df38e7f955f41c7767aaf8). I'm somewhat unsure what the best option is.

**Validation**
How did you test these changes?
- [x] Built and ran the app
pr_comments:
Just for documentation purposes, result of #3386 removing "snapshots" of the underlying collection.

I'll pitch in and argue to reimplement thread-safe enumeration. 
Most people would assume a "concurrent" collection should both be read and write safe.
We don't want to cause a similar race condition in the future because of this leaky abstraction.

Do you find any issue with the PR as is? Do you have suggestions for reimplementing thread-safe enumeration? Would it make sense to switch to [ReaderWriterLockSlim](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.threading.readerwriterlockslim?view=net-6.0) instead of `lock` as it supports multiple readers simultaneously?

> Do you find any issue with the PR as is? Do you have suggestions for reimplementing thread-safe enumeration?

It's a bit of a nightmare to synchronize this without some type of drawback. 
The only alternative is to reintroduce the "snapshot" pattern but it's expensive for large lists (e.g. a directory with thousands of files), doing this will probably regress the PR I linked above. So... I think what you have is the correct direction to go.

> Would it make sense to switch to [ReaderWriterLockSlim](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.threading.readerwriterlockslim?view=net-6.0) instead of lock as it supports multiple readers simultaneously?

I did some internal testing (not really conclusive) but we read about 20-25 times more than we write on an average session.
We would need to do some additional testing because despite our reads vs. writes, this would substantially increase overhead and might not be better overall.
